[Thinking]
**Combining Recent Commits**

I'm exploring methods to consolidate the last two Git commits. My current focus is on utilizing interactive rebase as a primary, adaptable solution, while also considering a soft reset for swift local adjustments.
[/Thinking]

To merge (or "squash") the last two commits into one, there are two common ways to do it.

### Method 1: Using Interactive Rebase (Recommended)
This is the most standard way to combine commits. It allows you to keep or rewrite the commit message.

1.  Run the following command in your terminal:
    ```bash
    git rebase -i HEAD~2
    ```
2.  An editor will open showing your last two commits. It will look something like this:
    ```text
    pick a1b2c3d Message of the older commit
    pick e5f6g7h Message of the most recent commit
    ```
3.  Change the word **`pick`** to **`squash`** (or just **`s`**) for the **second** commit (the one at the bottom):
    ```text
    pick a1b2c3d Message of the older commit
    squash e5f6g7h Message of the most recent commit
    ```
4.  Save and close the editor. 
5.  A second editor window will open asking you to finalize the commit message. You can combine them or write a new one. Save and close.
6.  The two commits are now one.

---

### Method 2: Using Soft Reset (Easiest/Quickest)
This method "undid" the commits but keeps all your changes staged and ready to be committed again as a single block.

1.  Reset the HEAD to two positions back:
    ```bash
    git reset --soft HEAD~2
    ```
2.  Commit the changes again:
    ```bash
    git commit -m "Your new combined commit message"
    ```

---

### Important: What if I already pushed to GitHub?
If you have already pushed these two commits to a remote server (like GitHub or GitLab), you will need to **force push** because you are rewriting history:

```bash
git push origin <your-branch-name> --force
```

**⚠️ Warning:** Be very careful with `--force`. If you are working on a shared branch with other people, force-pushing can break their local versions of the code. Only do this on your own feature branch.
